newsitem.title: SWEDEN: Pricer share risky but cheap - magazine.
newsitem.headline: Pricer share risky but cheap - magazine.

text.p: Sweden's Pricer AB, whose shares soared in Stockholm on Wednesday, is well-placed for an expected explosion in demand for electronic pricing systems, Swedish business magazine Affarsvarlden said on Wednesday.
The magazine forecast Pricer would post a net profit of 200 to 300 million crowns soon after the year 2000. For 1996 Pricer posted a net loss of 221.3 million crowns.
"If Pricer meets half of its goal and they take a 50 percent market share, the company's turnover in 10 years will be 100 billion crowns," the magazine said.
"(This) is in line with Ericsson's current turnover, if we estimate the total market at 200 billion crowns."
At 1345 GMT Pricer was 48 crowns higher at 358 crowns.
Affarsvarlden said with a 20 percent margin, Pricer's profits would be 20 billion crowns and according, to their calculations, the share was priced cheap.
"Of course the risk is high, but Pricer has a complete product which the company already has buyers for, unlike other supposedly high growth companies on the market," it said.

Because it used different technology than its competitiors -- which include Canada's Telepanel, U.S. ERS, U.S. NCR, France's Sitour and Israel's Eldat -- Pricer's systems are more flexible, the magazine said.
"The competitors' technology is based on information flow via cables or radio signals. Capacity in such systems is significantly lower than in infra-red technique," it said.

"In addition, flexibility in the Pricer system is higher, and infra-red signals have a higher range than radio waves in a closed room, which means fewer infra-red senders are needed than antennae with the same capacity," Affarsvarlden said.
Pricer also holds a key patent for wireless transmission of electronic price information which is good in 35 countries until the year 2008.
